guidance.evidence_criterion: Read the complete definition, its alternatives, any marking or confirmation rule, and the operative confidentiality duty. For explicit identification, Entailment requires identification, marking, or confirmation to govern the protected information; Contradiction applies when unmarked information is protected through blanket categories, its nature, circumstances, or a reasonable-person test. Do not cite a marking subclause alone when an alternative protects unmarked information. For technical-only scope, Contradiction requires express inclusion of identifiable non-technical categories; a generic reference to confidential, proprietary, non-public, or business-related material does not by itself settle the exclusivity claim. For oral information, require language expressly covering oral or comparable non-tangible disclosure, or a rule expressly bringing such disclosure within protection; do not infer oral coverage merely from the word information or from discussions occurring. For confidentiality of the agreement or negotiations, require language covering the agreement, contractual arrangements, negotiation communications, or their existence together with an operative nondisclosure duty; confidentiality of contemplated discussions alone is insufficient. Cite the whole responsive definition when its opening language, list, and terminal modality jointly establish scope, but exclude illustrative categories that do not bear on the tested boundary. Return NotMentioned whenever the exact form, subject, or exclusivity issue remains unsettled.

Separate the triggering event, the disposition duty, any retention exception, and survival. For return or destruction upon termination, Entailment requires termination, expiration, failure to proceed, or an equivalent end-of-relationship event to trigger return or destruction; a demand-only right does not establish the stated termination trigger. For post-agreement possession, Entailment requires an express right or necessity to retain identified information after a return-or-destruction obligation; Contradiction requires an exhaustive return or destruction command covering all information and copies without a retention route. A bare return duty that does not resolve continued possession is NotMentioned. For survival, require express continuation after termination or expiration, not a general contract term, remedy, exception, or duration measured from disclosure. When a survival clause identifies obligations by section or subject, read and cite the referenced operative obligations as well as the survival language. Cite the complete triggering and disposition unit, including a qualification that changes whether retention is allowed, but omit certification or administrative language unless it changes the substantive result.

Test the specific act of creating or reproducing a copy. Entailment requires an operative authorization to make copies in stated circumstances. Contradiction applies to an operative prohibition on copying or reproduction, including a consent-qualified prohibition unless another clause affirmatively grants the relevant copying permission. Do not infer permission from authorized use, access, possession, recordkeeping, reducing information to writing, delivery of existing copies, or permission to retain one already-existing archival copy. Cite the actor, copying verb, modality, and any condition or exception that controls the prohibition or permission. If the document regulates related handling but never settles creation of copies, return NotMentioned.

Inspect exclusions and limitations on confidentiality obligations by provenance. An independent-development exception supports permissible development only when it says the receiving party developed the information independently, ordinarily without use of, access to, or reliance on protected information. A third-party-source exception supports permissible acquisition only when the receiving party may receive or lawfully obtain the information from a third party entitled to disclose it and free of the relevant confidentiality restriction. Do not infer either proposition from ownership, permitted use, general information categories, prior possession, or disclosure by the disclosing party to somebody else. Cite the governing exclusion introduction when it supplies the legal effect, plus the exact provenance prong and any material conditions or proof requirement. Return Contradiction only for an operative provision barring the specified route; otherwise use NotMentioned when that provenance is absent.

Identify who may disclose, the permitted recipient class, the information, purpose, need-to-know limit, and confidentiality conditions. For employees, Entailment follows from an express employee access or disclosure whitelist even when subject to need, training, written undertakings, or recipient responsibility. For third parties, Entailment requires an express permitted class beyond employees, such as agents, representatives, consultants, affiliates, or advisers. A general nondisclosure rule is not permission. Treat a clause that permits only employees, or merely requires the receiving party to seek discretionary approval before any outside disclosure, as opposing the broader third-party-sharing statement; do not convert restrictions into permissions. Cite the operative whitelist and every condition that defines eligibility or responsibility, but not unrelated security duties. If no clause resolves the relevant recipient class, return NotMentioned.

Look for an operative statement that disclosure or the agreement grants no license, title, interest, ownership right, immunity, or other right in the confidential information or associated intellectual property. Such non-grant language supports the hypothesis; retained ownership reinforces rather than contradicts it. Read any stated exception, but a limited right granted elsewhere does not erase an otherwise scoped no-license rule. An affirmative grant of rights in the confidential information opposes the hypothesis only to the extent it matches the stated object and recipient. Cite each independently operative ownership and non-grant sentence when both contribute to the conclusion, while omitting warranty or permitted-use language. If neither a grant nor non-grant is expressed, return NotMentioned.

Match the contractual actor, action, object, polarity, and trigger exactly. Limited use is supported by an operative sole-purpose or no-other-purpose restriction; cite the incorporated purpose definition when needed and all independently operative use restrictions, but not merely adjacent disclosure or security terms. Compelled-disclosure notice requires advance, prompt, or otherwise responsive notice or consultation triggered by legal, regulatory, court, or comparable compulsory disclosure; incident, breach, or loss reporting does not qualify. A no-reverse-engineering conclusion requires an express prohibition on reverse engineering the protected object and must not be inferred from no-license, ownership, no-copy, or limited-use language. No solicitation requires an express ban on soliciting or inducing the specified representatives or employees; restrictions on using names, contacting information sources, advertising, or ordinary disclosure do not settle it. For each hypothesis, an express permission for the same conduct opposes a prohibition, while silence or regulation of a neighboring act is NotMentioned. Cite the operative duty or permission with any definition, condition, exception, duration, or trigger necessary to delimit it.

Read the complete definition, every alternative route into protection, form rules, and the operative nondisclosure duty. For explicit identification, support requires an identification, marking, description, or confirmation regime covering every protected route; contextual identification can qualify, but a separate blanket, nature-based, circumstances-based, or reasonable-person catchall that protects unidentified information opposes the all-information claim. A list of examples is not itself an identification requirement. For technical-only scope, oppose only when the definition expressly includes identifiable non-technical subjects such as business, financial, personnel, contractual, customer, or marketing information; generic references to confidential, proprietary, non-public, or business-related information alone leave exclusivity unresolved. Oral coverage requires express oral, verbal, visual, observed, or comparable non-tangible disclosure language, or an oral-confirmation rule; do not infer it from a substantive information category or general communications. Agreement-confidentiality requires the agreement, its contents, contractual arrangements or communications, negotiations, or their existence to fall under an operative nondisclosure duty; contemplated discussions alone are insufficient. An express permission covering the same subject opposes the relevant prohibition; otherwise return NotMentioned. Cite the governing opening, responsive alternatives, terminal modality, and operative duty only when each changes the result; exclude illustrative categories unrelated to the tested boundary.

operations.rationale: Repairs repeated quantifier and form confusion: the answers missed governing identification alternatives, inferred oral coverage from unrelated categories, and overlooked agreement-content or communications clauses. It also preserves the observed distinction between concrete non-technical categories and generic broad descriptions.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Separate trigger, actor, disposition command, retention route, and survival. Return-or-destroy support requires termination, expiration, failure to proceed, cessation of services or the stated business purpose, or another express end-of-relationship event to activate a duty; a request or demand alone, even if exercisable at any time, does not establish that trigger. Survival requires express continuation after termination, expiration, or completion; a contract duration, remedy, severability rule, or enforceability provision is not survival. If survival is stated by section or subject, read and cite the referenced operative obligations with the survival clause. Post-agreement possession is supported whenever an express exception permits or requires retention after an otherwise applicable return-or-destruction duty, including an archival copy or retention because disposition is infeasible. It is opposed when the controlling unit exhaustively requires all information and copies to be returned or destroyed with no retention route. A bare return duty that does not settle later possession is NotMentioned. Cite the complete trigger-and-disposition unit and every qualification changing retention; omit certification or administrative text unless it narrows the substantive duty.

operations.rationale: The observations repeatedly treated demand-only duties as termination duties, treated contract duration or remedies as survival, and missed archival or infeasibility-based retention exceptions. This update separates those three legal questions and their citation units.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Inspect the receiving party's specific authority to make, reproduce, duplicate, or record a copy. Support requires affirmative operative permission, such as copying reasonably necessary for the stated purpose. A default prohibition on copying or reproduction opposes the hypothesis even when copying could occur with prior consent; a consent mechanism is not present permission unless another provision affirmatively authorizes the relevant copying. Do not infer creation authority from use, access, possession, recordkeeping, reducing information to writing, delivery or return of existing copies, or permission to retain one existing archival copy. When a prohibition contains an internal copying exception, cite both the prohibition and the exception if both define the permission; otherwise cite only the operative actor, copying verb, modality, and controlling condition. If the document addresses neighboring handling acts without settling creation of copies, return NotMentioned.

operations.rationale: Corrects false permissions inferred from unrelated use clauses, archival retention, and consent-qualified prohibitions, while preserving the genuine internal-purpose copying exception.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Read the governing exclusions or limitations and keep the two provenance routes separate. Independent-development support requires a clause saying the receiving party developed the information independently, normally without using, accessing, referring to, or relying on protected information. Prior possession, authorized use, a substantive information category, a warranty disclaimer, or receipt from another source does not establish development. Third-party-acquisition support requires receipt, disclosure, or lawful obtainment by the receiving party from a third party entitled to provide the information and not bound by the relevant restriction. A clause merely saying the disclosing party gave information to another person, or that information was independently developed, does not establish third-party acquisition. Cite the exclusion introduction when it supplies the consequence, the exact provenance prong, and any proof, no-use, lawful-source, or no-confidentiality condition. An express prohibition on the same route is Contradiction; absence of the exact route is NotMentioned.

operations.rationale: The solver repeatedly substituted prior knowledge, permitted use, warranties, third-party receipt, and disclosure by the discloser for independent development, and conflated the two provenance hypotheses.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Identify the disclosing actor, each expressly permitted recipient class, the information, purpose, need-to-know limitation, and confidentiality conditions. Because the employee hypothesis concerns some employees, a whitelist limited to necessary or authorized employees supports it; do not treat that limitation as opposition. For third parties, support requires at least one expressly permitted external or potentially external class, such as agents, representatives, consultants, advisers, affiliates, or another approved class. A whitelist containing such a class still supports the hypothesis when employees are listed alongside it and when need-to-know, written-undertaking, or recipient-liability conditions apply. A whitelist limited to employees, officers, or directors opposes the broader third-party-sharing statement, as does an operative outside-disclosure prohibition with no standing external-class exception. Merely allowing the recipient to request discretionary approval for a future outsider is not present permission. Read a general prohibition together with its exceptions before deciding. Cite the operative whitelist and every eligibility or responsibility condition that defines it; for opposition cite the restrictive unit establishing that outsiders are excluded, not unrelated security provisions.

operations.rationale: Repairs the largest relation-confusion cluster: conditional employee access was misread as prohibition, external agents and advisers were collapsed into employees, and employee-only or approval-only clauses were incorrectly treated as third-party permission.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Look for operative language that the agreement or disclosure grants the receiving party no license, title, interest, ownership, immunity, or other right in the confidential information or associated intellectual property. Express retained or exclusive ownership can support the no-right conclusion when it directly negates acquisition by the recipient; read scoped exceptions and any affirmative grant before deciding. An affirmative grant opposes the hypothesis only when it gives the receiving party a right in the same protected object. Do not infer a non-grant from a confidentiality definition, nondisclosure duty, permitted-use restriction, entire-agreement clause, remedy, disclaimer, or no-warranty language. Cite every independently operative ownership or non-grant sentence that contributes to the conclusion, but exclude warranty, accuracy, commercialization, or administrative language unless it itself grants or withholds the relevant right. If neither a grant nor a non-grant is expressed, return NotMentioned.

operations.rationale: The answers invented no-license conclusions from entire-agreement, definition, and warranty language and sometimes cited adjacent disclaimers, while the original evidence distinguishes those clauses from operative retained-ownership or non-grant terms.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Match actor, conduct, object, polarity, trigger, duration, and exceptions exactly. Limited use is supported only by an operative sole-purpose, necessary-purpose, or no-other-purpose restriction; nondisclosure, confidentiality, ownership, or a definition alone does not restrict use. Cite all independently operative use restrictions and any incorporated purpose or exception needed to delimit them, but omit adjacent security and disclosure provisions. Compelled-disclosure notice requires notice or consultation responsive to a legal, regulatory, court, governmental, or comparable compulsory demand; breach, loss, incident, or unauthorized-disclosure reporting is not equivalent. Cite the compulsory-disclosure trigger and notice duty, plus a governing exception introduction only when it supplies their legal effect. Reverse engineering requires an express prohibition on reverse engineering, disassembly, decompilation, or an expressly equivalent act directed to the protected object; never infer it from identifiability, privacy, no-copy, ownership, no-license, or limited-use terms. No solicitation requires an express prohibition on soliciting, inducing, enticing, employing, or retaining the specified employees or representatives; contacting sources, using names, advertising, or disclosure restrictions do not qualify. Express permission for the same conduct is Contradiction; neighboring regulation or silence is NotMentioned. Include a qualification or duration only when it changes the responsive duty.

operations.rationale: Addresses the observed reverse-engineering inference from privacy text, compelled-disclosure confusion with incident reporting, limited-use inference from nondisclosure alone, and incomplete citation of purpose, exception, or duration language.
